newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar falls vs yen due to strong Tokyo stocks.
newsitem.headline: Dollar falls vs yen due to strong Tokyo stocks.

text.p: *Dollar eased against yen in mid-morning Tokyo partly on sales by interbank dealers in reaction to strong Tokyo stock market, dealers said.
*Tokyo Nikkei 225 average rose through 20,000 barrier in early morning trade for first time since December 1996.
*By 0117 GMT, the 225-share Nikkei average had climbed 510.55 points to 20,025.30.
*But support seen near 126.50 yen with bids from Japanese investors.
*But long-term credit bank dealer said dollar remains firm as long as steady bids from Japanese investors continue to emerge on downside.

*Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference that G7 nations agreed to pay utmost attention to dealing with movements in financial markets and currency rates while keeping close cooperative ties. No apparent impact was detected in currency markets. *Mitsuzuka said: "We have dealt with the issue in a stronger way than what was agreed at the G7's meeting in Berlin (in February)."
*Dollar up in early Tokyo on commercial buying ahead of 0100 GMT local fixing and expected to be well-bid until that time, with importers likely to be eager buyers in wake of Monday market holiday.
*Activity likely to taper off after 0100 GMT amid lack of fresh factors, with little buying expected from investors.
*Offers from exporters from around 127 yen up to keep gains capped.
